\begin{theorem}[Squared norm after a constant shift]
\lean{FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sub_const_sq}
\label{FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sub_const_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformLpNorm, FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_eq_expect_sq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ have uniform mean
zero, and let $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$. Then the squared uniform $L^2$ norm of $X-\theta$
is the squared uniform $L^2$ norm of $X$ plus $\theta^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Translated anticoncentration bound]
\lean{FABL.translated_anticoncentration_normalized}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p248-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p249-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p249-b006
}
\label{FABL.translated_anticoncentration_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsHypercontractiveRandomVariable, FABL.pmfEventProbability_uniformPMF_eq_uniformProbability, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.pmfPaleyZygmund, FABL.translated_fourthMoment_le, FABL.uniformLpNorm, FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_eq_expect_sq, FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sub_const_sq, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have uniform mean
zero and uniform $L^2$ norm one. Suppose $\rho>0$ and, for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the
uniform $L^4$ norm of $x\mapsto a+\rho bX(x)$ is at most the uniform $L^2$ norm of
$x\mapsto a+bX(x)$. For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $0<t<1$, the uniform probability that
$|X(x)-\theta|>t$ is at least
$\left(\frac{\rho^2(1-t^2)+\rho^2\theta^2}{1+\rho^2\theta^2}\right)^2$.
\end{theorem}
